Power Calculation for Bland-Altman Limits of Agreement

Source: R/power_agreement_limit.R
power_agreement_limit.Rd

Computes the sample size, power, maximal allowable difference, or standard deviation for a method comparison study analyzed with the Bland-Altman limits of agreement, using the method of Lu et al. (2016). Agreement is concluded when the confidence intervals of both limits of agreement fall within [-delta, delta].

Usage

power_agreement_limit(
  n = NULL,
  delta = NULL,
  mu = 0,
  sigma = NULL,
  power = NULL,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  agree.level = 0.95,
  m = 1,
  icc = 0
)

Arguments

n

Number of pairs (sample size), or the number of subjects when m > 1.

delta

Maximal allowable difference: the methods agree if the confidence limits of the limits of agreement lie within [-delta, delta].

mu

Mean of the paired differences (default 0).

sigma

Standard deviation of the paired differences. With clustered data (m > 1), the total SD of the differences.

power

Target power.

conf.level

Confidence level of the confidence intervals of the limits of agreement (default 0.95).

agree.level

Agreement level of the limits of agreement: the proportion of differences the limits should contain (default 0.95).

m

number of paired measurements per subject (default 1, independent pairs). See the "Clustered data" section.

icc

intraclass correlation of the paired differences (between-subject share of the variance of the differences), in [0, 1). Ignored when m = 1. This is not the test-retest ICC of the measurements themselves.

Value

An object of class "power.htest", a list with components:

n

Sample size (pairs, or subjects when m > 1)

delta

Maximal allowable difference

mu

Mean of differences

sigma

Standard deviation of differences

conf.level

Confidence level of the CIs of the limits of agreement

agree.level

Agreement level of the limits of agreement

power

Power of the procedure

m, icc

The clustering inputs

n.obs

Total number of pairs, n * m

method

Description of the method

note

Additional notes

Details

Specify three of n, delta, sigma, and power; the fourth is calculated.

The limits of agreement are mu +/- z \* sigma, with z the (1 + agree.level) / 2 quantile of the standard normal, and their confidence intervals are those of Bland and Altman (1999), with standard error sigma \* sqrt(1/n + z^2 / (2 (n - 1))). This is the interval from agreement_limit() with loa_calc = "blandaltman". The power is Lu et al. (2016), eq. 5:

power = 1 - T(t, n - 1, tau1) - T(t, n - 1, tau2),

where T is the CDF of the non-central t distribution, t is the 1 - (1 - conf.level) / 2 quantile of the central t distribution with n - 1 df, tau1 = (delta - mu - z \* sigma) / SE, and tau2 = (delta + mu - z \* sigma) / SE. Negative values are set to 0. These are the values reported by PASS (Chapter 427), which notes that the sample sizes in Table 1 of Lu et al. (2016), based on their approximate eq. 6, are sometimes slightly too large.

A sample size can only be found when the true limits of agreement lie within the bounds, i.e. |mu| + z \* sigma < delta; otherwise power goes to 0 as n increases and an error is returned.

With clustered data (m > 1), the standard error of the limits uses the effective sample size n \* m / (1 + (m - 1) \* icc) for the mean difference and a Satterthwaite df for the SD, under a balanced compound symmetry model (see agree_expected_half() for the model). This is an approximation; m = 1 gives the original results.

For a power curve over a range of sample sizes, see blandPowerCurve().

References

Lu, M. J., et al. (2016). Sample Size for Assessing Agreement between Two Methods of Measurement by Bland-Altman Method. The International Journal of Biostatistics, 12(2). doi:10.1515/ijb-2015-0039

Bland, J. M., and Altman, D. G. (1999). Measuring agreement in method comparison studies. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 8(2), 135-160. doi:10.1177/096228029900800204

NCSS (PASS Sample Size Software). Chapter 427: Bland-Altman Method for Assessing Agreement in Method Comparison Studies.

See also

blandPowerCurve(), power_agreement_exact(), agree_expected_half(), agreement_limit()

Examples

# Sample size for 80% power (PASS Example 1: n = 60)
power_agreement_limit(delta = 7, mu = 0.5, sigma = 2.5, power = 0.80)
#> 
#>      Power for Bland-Altman Limits of Agreement (Lu et al. 2016) 
#> 
#>               n = 60
#>           delta = 7
#>              mu = 0.5
#>           sigma = 2.5
#>      conf.level = 0.95
#>     agree.level = 0.95
#>           power = 0.8059154
#>               m = 1
#>             icc = 0
#>           n.obs = 60
#> 
#> NOTE: H0: CIs of the 95% limits of agreement not within [-delta, delta]
#>      H1: CIs of the limits of agreement within [-delta, delta]
#>      n is the number of pairs. Two measurements per unit; one for each method.
#> 

# Power at a given sample size (PASS Example 2)
power_agreement_limit(n = 201, delta = 2.5, mu = 0.2, sigma = 1)
#> 
#>      Power for Bland-Altman Limits of Agreement (Lu et al. 2016) 
#> 
#>               n = 201
#>           delta = 2.5
#>              mu = 0.2
#>           sigma = 1
#>      conf.level = 0.95
#>     agree.level = 0.95
#>           power = 0.800283
#>               m = 1
#>             icc = 0
#>           n.obs = 201
#> 
#> NOTE: H0: CIs of the 95% limits of agreement not within [-delta, delta]
#>      H1: CIs of the limits of agreement within [-delta, delta]
#>      n is the number of pairs. Two measurements per unit; one for each method.
#> 

# Largest SD for which 90% power is reached with 100 pairs
power_agreement_limit(n = 100, delta = 7, mu = 0.5, power = 0.90)
#> 
#>      Power for Bland-Altman Limits of Agreement (Lu et al. 2016) 
#> 
#>               n = 100
#>           delta = 7
#>              mu = 0.5
#>           sigma = 2.577867
#>      conf.level = 0.95
#>     agree.level = 0.95
#>           power = 0.9
#>               m = 1
#>             icc = 0
#>           n.obs = 100
#> 
#> NOTE: H0: CIs of the 95% limits of agreement not within [-delta, delta]
#>      H1: CIs of the limits of agreement within [-delta, delta]
#>      n is the number of pairs. Two measurements per unit; one for each method.
#> 

# Clustered data, 3 pairs per subject, ICC of the differences 0.15
power_agreement_limit(delta = 7, mu = 0.5, sigma = 2.5, power = 0.80,
                      m = 3, icc = 0.15)
#> 
#>      Power for Bland-Altman Limits of Agreement (Lu et al. 2016) 
#> 
#>               n = 23
#>           delta = 7
#>              mu = 0.5
#>           sigma = 2.5
#>      conf.level = 0.95
#>     agree.level = 0.95
#>           power = 0.8119145
#>               m = 3
#>             icc = 0.15
#>           n.obs = 69
#> 
#> NOTE: H0: CIs of the 95% limits of agreement not within [-delta, delta]
#>      H1: CIs of the limits of agreement within [-delta, delta]
#>      n is the number of subjects, each with m = 3 paired measurements (n.obs pairs in total).
#>      Assumes balanced compound symmetry with ICC of the differences = 0.15.
#>
